biography: Aldoir Sette's journey began amidst the vibrant chaos of São Paulo's karting scene. Unlike many of his peers who came from privileged backgrounds, Aldoir's family ran a small auto repair shop. His passion ignited watching Ayrton Senna on a battered television screen in the workshop. He saved every spare Real to buy used tires and enter local kart races, often arriving late after helping his father. His aggressive style, honed on the streets, quickly earned him attention, though his inconsistent performances often frustrated potential sponsors. A defining moment was winning the Brazilian Karting Championship in 2005 with a borrowed engine. After a brief stint in Formula Renault, he found a home in Brazilian endurance racing, piloting the MetalMoro MRX P2. Now a veteran at 38, Aldoir struggles to recapture his early promise, battling younger drivers and the ever-present inconsistency that has plagued his career. He still hopes for a major international opportunity before he hangs up his helmet, a dream fueled by the memory of Senna's unwavering determination.
drivingStyle: Aldoir's driving style is a blend of raw aggression and calculated risk. He is known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, often flirting with the edge of control. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it also leads to costly mistakes. Tire management is not his strong suit, preferring to maximize pace in short bursts rather than conserve rubber over a long stint. Under pressure, Aldoir tends to become more erratic, either producing moments of brilliance or unforced errors.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Salles
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their karting days. Ricardo always had the best equipment, fueling Aldoir's resentment and determination to beat him.

rivalries.name: Isabela Vieira
rivalries.reason: A fierce competitor in the Brazilian endurance scene. Their on-track battles are legendary, often resulting in close calls and heated exchanges in the paddock.

rivalries.name: Jair Bolsonaro (fictional driver)
rivalries.reason: A constant source of friction due to conflicting driving styles and numerous on-track collisions. They represent the old guard versus the new generation.

quirks: Always wears a lucky wristband made by his grandmother before every race.
Refuses to eat anything yellow on race days.
Visits the grave of Ayrton Senna every year on the anniversary of his death.
famousQuote: "Sometimes you have to risk it all to win, even if it means ending up in the barrier."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2012 Mil Milhas Brasil at Interlagos, overcoming a late-race penalty to secure a dramatic victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2015 24 Hours of Interlagos with just 30 minutes remaining, costing his team a certain victory.
